newsitem.title: USA: Occidental says Colombian repairs stalled.
newsitem.headline: Occidental says Colombian repairs stalled.

text.p: Colombian work crews set to repair the dynamite-damaged Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline are waiting for the military to secure the region before starting work, an Occidental Petroleum Corp spokesman said Wednesday.
The spokesman said the army appeared to be shaken and proceeding with extra caution after suffering heavy casualties in trying to secure the area after two recent explosions.

Crude production from the 180,000 barrel per day Cano Limon field remained shut-in Wednesday, marking the tenth day of output delays following repeated pipeline bombings by leftist National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas.
"Typically, these pipeline repairs take around 24 to 48 hours but the army has to secure the area first," said Larry Mariage, spokesman for Occidental in Bakersfield, California.
"We haven't had any indication from the army yet when that might happen. I think they are a little shaken," said Mariage.

The army suffered most of the 20 casualties recently when a helicopter was shot down when on a mission into the area where one of the recent explosions occured. Another 11 soldiers were killed when a column on its way to a damaged site was attacked, Mariage said.

On Tuesday, Occidental was forced to declare force majeure on the Cano Limon field, laying off workers. Ecopetrol, the state oil company, also declared force majeure on the delivery of two crude shipments due to be dispatched from the Caribbean coast lifting terminal at Covenas earlier in the month.
"Really, the ball is in the court of the Colombian military to effect repairs...we have to deal with this like any other foreign entity, waiting like everybody else," said Mariage.
Occidental operates the Cano Limon field, holding an 18 percent share, with Royal Dutch Shell Group and Ecopetrol sharing the remaining interest.
The Cano Limon pipeline has been attacked 38 times this year alone, and a total of 47 times in 1996. Since coming into operation in 1986, the line has been attacked some 474 times.
The latest series of attacks has forced the first force majeure on Cano Limon liftings since 1992, Occidental said.
